content:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a reproducible tail-latency regression in the replay harness vs synthetic on a small subset of jobs. Looks related to KV cache churn + mmap behavior on H100 with driver 535.x. Can we triage?
priya: rough numbers? is this only H100 or showing on A100 too?
alex: mainly H100. Synthetic bench steady ~18ms p50, replay shows occasional spikes to 180-400ms p99 for long contexts (~8k tokens). Quick flamegraph points at a lot of time in page-fault / uvm_fault_handler paths.
chris: uvm faults would indicate some mmap/uvm pinning issue. Did the container image change recently?
alex: yep — we bumped base image to ubuntu:22.04 + cudnn/cuda layers matching driver 535. Driver package used: 535.113.01. Also changed the kernel cmdline to include "transparent_hugepage=madvise" in the image build as part of perf hardening.
kevin: @alex can you paste the perf record snippet? even a small sample helps.
alex: sure — here's a small stack dump from perf (replay run):
```
# samples from perf
uvm_fault_handler+0x40
__handle_mm_fault+0x120
do_page_fault+0x80
handle_mm_fault+0x150
kv_cache_lookup
kv_cache_miss_handler
runtime::serve_token_batch
```
priya: that looks like kernel-side page faults during cache access. Are we seeing any OOM/killer events or dmesg messages?
alex: dmesg shows repeated: "nv_peer_mem: uvm_map_user_pages failed" and a few "page pinning failed: -12" when spikes occur.
chris: -12 is -ENOMEM from pin_user_pages. Might be interaction between RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in the container and the changed kernel flags. If page pinning fails, we fallback and cause user-space page faults.
jen: infra-bot ran an image diff yesterday when the base was updated. infra-bot: image-diff report: image-layer: cuda-12.2/cudnn-9 bump, kernel-cmdline flags altered, glibc patch 2.35->2.36. No explicit rlimit changes.
infra-bot: deploy-notes: some nodes still on driver 535.54, others on 535.113.01; node labels: h100-v2 and h100-v2b.
kevin: heterogenous driver versions + kernel flag diffs are a classic source. For page pinning, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in container must be high enough; also KSM/THP can cause fragmentation. Can we run a quick repro with memlock upped?
alex: tried scc-run with `ulimit -l unlimited` and pinned mem, p99 drops from ~300ms to ~40ms in one trial. That strongly implicates pinning.
priya: interesting. Is synthetic load using the same replay IO pattern? maybe synthetic uses cold starts and smaller working set so no pins.
chris: exactly — synthetic often streams short sequences so KV working set stays small. Replay replays user traces with multi-hit KV accesses causing more pinned pages needed.
kevin: propose steps: 1) run targeted repro on h100-v2b with driver 535.113.01, memlock unlimited, same container image; 2) run on h100-v2 (535.54) to check driver delta; 3) capture perf + /proc/vmstat + `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `cat /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` false positives; 4) try kernel cmdline without THP change.
jen: I can repro step 1 on a staging pool. Scheduling it now — job id staging-repro-2131.
alex: thanks. also added a short trace showing KV cache churn counters: `kv_hits=1.2M kv_misses=87k page_pin_fail=1234` during one bad window.
priya: can you paste the command for the replay harness run so I can run locally?
alex: run: `./replay_harness --trace traces/2026-03-longctx.json --concurrency 8 --model rdx-13b --profile perf.data`
chris: small note — kernel 5.15 vs 6.x changes UVM behavior; what kernel versions on the two node classes?
infra-bot: node h100-v2: kernel 5.15.102, driver 535.54. h100-v2b: kernel 6.1.48, driver 535.113.01.
kevin: that explains it — newer kernel + driver + THP changes can interact badly for paged pinned memory. Good we've reproduced with memlock tweak. Next we should decide: require memlock in our pod spec for private/dedicated, or add a guard in runtime to pre-pin KV pages.
priya: pre-pinning KV pages at runtime may reduce flexibility and increase startup time. Policy-wise, requiring RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in deployment templates (and documenting) seems cleaner. But we need an operational fallback: if pin fails, degrade gracefully not cause page faults and p99 spikes.
alex: I can prototype a fallback: on pin fail, we switch to a small prefetch window and use async readback to avoid sync faults — will instrument counters.
jen: tagging infra to roll a driver-consistency check across fleets. @kevin can you add a short checklist for required kernel/driver combos for our dedicated fleet?
kevin: will do — checklist will include min driver 535.54+, kernel >=5.15 or specific backports, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK >= 512MB, THP ADVISED off for kernels that misbehave, and container image base pinned to ubuntu:22.04-cuda12.2.
chris: also add an eval harness test: replay long-context with memlock=unlimited and memlock=small to detect regressions automatically.
alex: I'll open a follow-up PR with the runtime fallback and instrumentation.
priya: thanks. one last thing — let's capture exact perf counters and a short guide for SRE on how to triage page-pin related spikes. Can someone draft that?
kevin: I'll draft SRE triage notes and post here by EOD.
jen: staging job completed: staging-repro-2131 logs uploaded to shared bucket s3://redwood-staging/repro/2131.
alex: added a short blob with perf.data and `perf script` output to the bucket. Link: https://s3.redwood/repro/2131/perf.tgz
priya: awesome. feel free to ping me when the PR is up, I'll review the instrumentation. :thumbsup:
